analysis:
Examined all supplied metadata, patches and base/head source for the workflow and two documentation files against the canonical definition index and selected detailed boundaries. No concrete security regression was identified. .github/workflows/release-desktop.yml:142 signs the DMG before notarization using the existing fingerprint-selected Developer ID and temporary keychain (111–118). Lines 172–176 add signature verification, expected-team enforcement and an explicit Notarized Developer ID check. Existing notarization acceptance, stapling, app validation and image integrity checks remain; set -euo pipefail preserves failure propagation through the new tee pipeline. Hash generation and publication follow verification (179–210), and keychain cleanup remains unchanged (212–215). No new credentials, workflow triggers, permissions or external endpoints are introduced.

The changes strengthen artifact integrity relevant to T-013/T-034 without treating container signing as App Attest qualification or serving authorization (A-017, T-054, TB-011). Provider key custody, inference encryption, plaintext handling, billing, cancellation, cache storage and privileged helper behavior are unchanged in this supplied scope. docs/operations/desktop-release.md:57–58 accurately reflects the new checks and retains the separate hardware-qualification limitation at 71–72; changelog.d/desktop-release-sign-dmg.md:3–5 describes the same change. Its historical dry-run claim was not independently verified and is not relied on for the security conclusion. Build internals, installer behavior and platform authorization implementations were not supplied or audited; the PR does not change their contracts in the examined evidence.
